lines.meet: Ciao, I'm Gianluca, a guardian, which means I stand in front and talk. You'll get used to the talking, everybody does, eventually.
lines.meet_neighbour: Steamwheedle Port, of course, you're the one who walks past my fire every evening and never stops! I'm Gianluca, and now you'll have to stop.
lines.ask_home: Allora, which city's yours? Tell me, and I'll tell you what they do wrong with the coffee there.
lines.ask_work: And before all this, what were you? Wait, let me guess first, I'm good at this, thirty years behind a bar.
lines.answer_home: Bologna, near the university. The best food in Italy, and I'll argue that with anybody, especially somebody from Milan.
lines.answer_work: I ran my parents' bar for thirty years, open at six for the people going to work and late for the people avoiding going home.
lines.chat_food: Mortadella, sliced so thin you can read through it, with a glass of something red. Mamma mia, I'd give this whole world for a plate of it.
lines.chat_sleep: I sleep four hours, like a barman, and the rest of the time I'm talking. People ask when I rest, and I say I'm resting now.
lines.chat_missing: The six o'clock crowd, who never ordered, because I already knew. That's the best feeling there is, knowing what somebody wants before they ask.
lines.chat_here: I've rated every coffee substitute on this world out of ten. The best so far is a four, and I was generous.
lines.tease_quiet: Dai, say something, {name}! I've been talking for both of us since breakfast, and my voice is getting tired.
lines.tease_talker: Finally, somebody who talks as much as I do! Mamma mia, {name}, we're going to have to take turns.
lines.tease_careful: You test the coffee before you drink it, {name}, like it might be poison. With what they serve here, you're right.
lines.tease_bold: You'd drink an espresso standing up in one go, {name}, like a real Italian. I approve, and I worry.
lines.tease_any: I know your drink, {name}, I've known it since the first day. That's how I know we're friends.
lines.tease_back: Ha, allora, {name}, that's a good one! You've been listening to me, that's the problem.
lines.take_it_kindly: Mamma mia, {name}, you're right, and my wife would say the same. I'll shut up for one minute.
lines.bristle: Ehi, not that one, {name}, please. Pick anything else.
lines.apologise: Scusa, scusa, I talked before I thought, which is the trouble with talking all day. I'm sorry, really.
lines.double_down: Allora, that stays said. Thirty years behind a bar, I know when somebody needs telling.
lines.needle_quiet: You sit there with a face like a cold coffee and never say what's wrong. How am I supposed to fix it?
lines.needle_talker: Even I can't get a word in with you, and I talk for a living. Give somebody else a turn.
lines.needle_careful: You've been deciding for twenty minutes. In my bar, the coffee would be cold and the customer would have left.
lines.needle_bold: You run in like a drunk at closing time, and I'm the one who has to stand in front of you.
lines.needle_any: You won't sit down, you won't eat, you won't talk to anybody. You'd have been the worst customer I ever had.
lines.bite_back: I've stood in front of you all and never complained once. Well, I complained, but I stood there.
lines.hurt: Mamma mia, that's the first time in thirty years somebody's made me stop talking. I'll be quiet now.
lines.laugh_off: Ha, a regular of mine was ruder than that every morning for twenty years, and he still tipped. Dai, let's go.
lines.confide: {name}, I read the Milan list twice every time I go to a hub, for my boys. I tell everybody they moved away and I took it personally. Don't tell anyone I read it twice.
lines.listen: Allora, {name}, I'll stop talking now, look. I'm listening, and it stays with me.
lines.look_out: Behind my shield in there, {name}, and don't argue. I'll talk the whole time so you know where I am.
lines.accept: Va bene, {name}, your way. Don't get used to me agreeing.
lines.deflect: Ehi, it's nothing, {name}, it's a bruise. Look after somebody who's actually bleeding.
lines.check_in: Talk to me, {name}, where did it get you? And no jokes, that's my job.
lines.blame: Somebody wouldn't stay behind the shield, and now look at us. I'm not naming names, but I'm looking at you.
lines.thank: Mamma mia, you brought me back, and I was halfway gone. Grazie, there's a coffee for you every morning forever.
lines.brush_off: Ah, prego, prego, sit down. I'll make you something, it'll be terrible, but it'll be warm.
lines.worry: Mamma mia, {name}, I thought we'd lost you! Sit down, sit, and don't you move.
lines.handed_down: Allora, I'm wearing yours now, I think. It'll be treated like my espresso machine.
lines.hand_fine: Take it, take it, it's yours now! I've got the shield and my mouth, that's all I need.
lines.hand_sulk: Ehi, nobody even asked me about that. It's the principle of the thing.
lines.turn_friendly: You're one of my regulars now, {name}. I know your drink, and you don't have to order.
lines.turn_friends: When I open the bar, {name}, you're getting a stool with your name on it. That's family, in Bologna.
lines.turn_grating: Allora, it isn't working between us, and I get along with everybody. That's a first for me.
lines.turn_rivals: I'll stand in front of you because that's what a guardian does. I won't make you a coffee, though.
lines.make_up: Dai, {name}, enough of this. Come and sit by my fire, I'll make something, and we'll start again.
lines.defend: Ehi, ehi, leave it. {name} was doing fine, and you know it.
lines.friend_left: Mamma mia, it's quiet with {name} away. Even I've stopped talking, nearly.
lines.friend_back: {name}, ciao, ciao! Sit down, I knew you'd be back, I've had your drink ready.
lines.common_kitchen: I cooked behind my bar for thirty years, and I've got opinions about every dish on this world. You know your way round a kitchen too, I can smell it.
lines.common_hosts: Thirty years of opening at six and knowing everybody's order. Somebody who's run a place for people knows the best feeling is a stranger becoming a regular.
lines.common_italian: You speak Italian! Finally, somebody who understands that coffee is serious, so tell me where you're from, and please don't say Milan.
lines.common_parent: My two boys moved to Milan, both of them, and I took it personally. They rang every Sunday, and I still listen for it.
